h: Ten Divine Garments Reveal the Order of Israel’s Redemption

p: and corresponding to them HaKadosh Baruch Hu put on
And it is known that everywhere
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג יא, ב)
along the lines of what it says (Zohar III 11b):
"Ten utterances in the work of Creation
and ten utterances at Matan Torah."
And these are the ten garments
that is, His emanating the ten sefiros
for the creation of the world.
And it counts there two garments
that He put on to exact retribution from the kingdom of Greece:
'And He put on righteousness as a coat of mail,
and a helmet of salvation on His head.'"
וְהֵם כְּנֶגֶד מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּהַפְטוֹרָה זוֹ
And they correspond to what is said in this haftarah:
"For He has clothed me in garments of salvation;
He has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness";
which correspond to Mashiach ben Yosef
שֶׁהֵם מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם
who are chariots for the middah of "the tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
Only that here in the haftarah
which corresponds to the middah of Malchus;
for such is the order in the ten sefiros:
which speaks of the garments of Hashem Yisbarach,
for such is the order of conquest
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach:
and afterward "a helmet of salvation on His head."
which darkened the eyes of Yisrael
for it is stated (Zohar Chadash, Yisro):
this is the kingdom of Greece,
but the brightness is not in them,
because there is none among all the kingdoms
that are close to the path of faith
they are the root of heresy and apikorsus,
And it is "one opposite the other,"
against the light of the Oral Torah.
And not like the wisdom of Egypt,
which was sorcery and the like,
which was through the power of impurity,
and it stood opposite the Written Torah in holiness
And the victory over the kingdom of Greece
הוּא עַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
is through the power of the Oral Torah,
פֶּה תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה קָרֵינַן לָהּ
"Mouth — we call her the Oral Torah."
Tzedek is the holy Malchus, as is known,
and the hei is also the middah of Malchus,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעח, ב)
"The hei was a dalet at first,
and once it was impregnated with a yud within it," etc.
That is, the yud of the Name Havayah
and the yud of the Name Adnus
through the yud of the Name Shakai,
that issues from within the holy upper yud
and then the letter hei is formed,
which alludes to the middah of Malchus
(and this was explained for Rosh Chodesh Elul);
and this is "And He put on righteousness as a coat of mail."
And when wisdom enters the heart,
then one merits the aspect of Daas,
then "and knowledge will be pleasant to your soul";
and Daas is the inwardness of Kesser Elyon,
And this is what is said:
"and a helmet of salvation on His head,"
which is the aspect of Kesser Elyon;
and this comes through the middah of Yesod,
of which Moshe Rabbeinu and Aharon
Moshe, the groomsman of the King,
who brought down the Written Torah from Heaven,
and Aharon, the groomsman of the Queen,
to bring wisdom into the heart of Yisrael
עָתִיד לִלְבּוֹשׁ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְכוּלֵּי
HaKadosh Baruch Hu is destined to put on," etc.:
"to exact retribution from Gog and Magog:
And both are mentioned in this haftarah,
and they correspond to Yesod and Malchus,
שֶׁהוּא מֶרְכָּבָה לְמִדַּת צַדִּיק יְסוֹד עוֹלָם
who is a chariot for the middah of "the tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
who is a chariot for the middah of Malchus.
and to the victory over the nations of the world
and the conquest of the wicked kingdom;
and corresponding to this is the pasuk,
to exact retribution from Gog and Magog,
corresponds to the middah of Malchus;
and corresponding to this is the pasuk,
"This one, glorious in His apparel," etc.,
And as it counted for the first garment:
"You have put on glory and splendor" (Tehillim 104:1);
And likewise there are mentioned in this Pesikta
in which Yisrael are called a bride
(if we count those of Yeshayahu as the last,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּחְשָׁב בַּגְּמָרָא בָּבָא בַּתְרָא יד, ב)
as they are counted in the Gemara, Bava Basra 14b):
and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels";
"And as a groom rejoices over a bride,
so will your God rejoice over you."
correspond to the middos of Yesod and Malchus:
"as a bride adorns herself with her jewels,"
which are the adornments of a bride,
corresponds to the middah of "the tzaddik, foundation of the world,"
who is called "of beautiful form and beautiful appearance";
for the intent is a fine body,
clean of blemish of the covenant.
וְכֵן מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פד, א)
And likewise what they said (Bava Metzia 84a):
of the beautiful ones of Yerushalayim," etc.;
the intent is not physical beauty,
but a body clean of this blemish;
and resembling the beauty of Yaakov,
"my strength and the first of my vigor,"
and he was like Adam HaRishon before the corruption,
of whom it is written, "and they were not ashamed";
for he knew nothing of bodily pleasure,
And this is "and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels,"
"And as a groom rejoices over a bride"
corresponds to the middah of Malchus,
this haftarah corresponds to the middah of Malchus,
and it is preparation for Rosh Hashanah,
וְתִמְלוֹךְ אַתָּה הוּא ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ לְבַדֶּךָ
"And You will reign, You, Hashem our God, alone."
